title: An ALMA Survey of CO Isotopologue Emission from Protoplanetary Disks in Chamaeleon I
question: Can CO isotopologue (13CO, C18O J=3-2) emission serve as an alternate probe of disk gas mass in Cha I disks, and what gas masses and gas-to-dust ratios result?

data.sensitivity: 1σ rms 30 (43) mJy/beam for 13CO (C18O) in Cool and 107 (126) mJy/beam in Hot sample at 0.25 km/s

what.value: Continuum flux densities, stellar masses, spectral types, phase-center offsets, dust masses

evidence.quote: continuum flux densities and stellar masses[^4] of our sample are adopted from (cite: pascucci2016)
Accretion rates are obtained from (cite: manara2016a; manara17)

what.value: Disk model grids for CO luminosity to gas mass conversion (MvD16)

evidence.quote: MvD16 developed hundreds of full thermal-chemical models that include isotope-selective photodissociation and CO freeze-out.
we derive the gas mass from WB14 model grids by adopting the same approach described in detail in (cite: ansdell2016)

recipe.method: CASA calibration with NRAO scripts, concat, uvcontsub, clean with natural weighting

recipe.goal: Define extraction region and velocity range by stacking
recipe.method: Stack images shifted to continuum centroid, weighted by noise; adopt 0.6'' radius (13CO), 0.3'' (C18O), 0-10 km/s
assumptions: C18O has same velocity range as 13CO

recipe.goal: Measure flux uncertainties and detection significance
recipe.method: Standard deviation of fluxes in 20 random apertures in each of six 10 km/s control ranges; mean adopted as uncertainty; 3σ detection threshold

recipe.goal: Measure fluxes for detections with adapted apertures
recipe.method: Increase circular aperture in 0.15'' steps on moment-0 map until flux flattens

recipe.goal: Fit 13CO flux vs stellar mass and continuum
recipe.method: Bayesian power-law fit F=β M*^α with chi2 likelihood including intrinsic scatter; Linmix and cenken as checks

recipe.goal: Convert line luminosities to gas masses
recipe.method: Fitted functions to median luminosity per mass bin of MvD16 grids (T Tauri, 1 Lsun); WB14 grids matched within uncertainties
assumptions: CO-to-H2 ~1e-4 ISM abundance; distance 188 pc; MvD16 T Tauri models with stellar luminosity 1 Lsun

recipe.goal: Compute gas-to-dust ratios and compare with Lupus
recipe.method: Gas mass over dust mass (Td=20 K, 188 pc); Kaplan-Meier and cendiff two-sample tests for Cha I vs Lupus over 10^4 iterations

evidence.quote: We detect $^{13}$CO emission from 17 out of 93 sources

answer_key.quantity: log F13CO vs log M* slope
log F13CO vs log Fmm slope

evidence.quote: The mean signals are 574$\pm$31 mJy km s$^{-1}$ in $^{13}$CO
yields a noise-weighted average line flux of 70$\pm$15 mJy km s$^{-1}$ in $^{13}$CO

answer_key.quantity: log Mgas vs log M* slope (MvD16)

evidence.quote: The median value of gas-to-dust ratio is $\sim 4$ when the gas mass is evaluated from MvD16
$\sim$ 0.07 M$_{\rm Jup}$ (22 M$_{\rm Earth}$) for the Hot sample

answer_key.quantity: Median P value Cha I vs Lupus 13CO flux

evidence.quote: with the median P value of 0.25

not_stated_but_needed: CASA version and clean parameters (cell size, image size, niter, threshold, mask)
Line-free channels used in uvcontsub and fit order
Priors ranges and emcee settings (walkers, steps) for the flux-stellar mass fit
Exact line-luminosity definition and unit conversion for MvD16 fits
Dust-mass values from Pascucci et al. needed for gas-to-dust ratios
missing_for_reproduction: Per-source dust masses from Pascucci et al. 2016
score_reason: Data public and flux method well described with tables, but imaging parameters and software versions missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, a described aperture-photometry recipe, and numeric flux and gas-mass tables.
